purpose: Few groups over a large table with HAVING (Hashed or parallel partial aggregation)
sql:
SELECT l_shipmode, avg(l_quantity) AS avg_qty, count(*) AS n
FROM lineitem
WHERE l_receiptdate > l_commitdate
GROUP BY l_shipmode
HAVING count(*) > 100000

extra.AI Reason: Aggregate by shipmode with a having clause filter on the count.
Full scan of lineitem is required to evaluate the receiptdate vs commitdate condition.

differences.text: PostgreSQL runs part of the plan in parallel (Gather Merge), with partial aggregation in each worker. The AI plan runs in a single process.

Aggregate (Sorted, Finalize) over (lineitem): PostgreSQL uses Sorted aggregation, the AI uses Hashed. Hashed aggregation needs no sorted input but more memory. Sorted aggregation needs sorted input but little memory. The AI's reason: "Aggregate by shipmode with a having clause filter on the count."
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Gather Merge over (lineitem) (collects sorted rows from parallel workers, keeping the order).
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Sort over (lineitem) (sorts its input).
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Aggregate (Hashed, Partial) over (lineitem) (computes aggregates (GROUP BY, SUM, COUNT, ...)).

similarities: Both plans use Seq Scan on lineitem.
